subtopics.title: Goodness of fit and contingency tables

command_words.Show that: Prove a given result; every step must be shown (answer given).
command_words.Hence: Use the previous result to reach the answer.
command_words.Hence or otherwise: Using the previous result is expected, but any valid method earns the marks.
command_words.Find: Work out; method marks need working.
command_words.Calculate: Work out from given facts; show working.
command_words.Sketch: Draw the shape with key features labelled (intercepts, asymptotes, turning points), not to scale.
command_words.Exact: Give the answer in surd, fraction, pi or ln form, not a decimal.
command_words.Verify: Show that given values satisfy the statement.
command_words.Interpret: Explain the meaning of a result in the context of the question.

kcs.title: Linear combinations of Normal variables
kcs.statement: Distribution of linear combinations of independent Normal random variables.
kcs.raw: Distribution of linear combinations of independent Normal random variables.
kcs.guidance: If $X \sim N(\mu_x, \sigma_x^2)$ and $Y \sim N(\mu_y, \sigma_y^2)$ independently, then $aX \pm bY \sim N(a\mu_x \pm b\mu_y,\ a^2\sigma_x^2 + b^2\sigma_y^2)$. No proofs required.

kcs.title: Simple random sampling
kcs.statement: Methods for collecting data. Simple random sampling. Use of random numbers for sampling.
kcs.raw: Methods for collecting data. Simple random sampling. Use of random numbers for sampling.

kcs.title: Stratified, systematic, quota sampling
kcs.statement: Other methods of sampling: stratified, systematic, quota.
kcs.raw: Other methods of sampling: stratified, systematic, quota.
kcs.guidance: The circumstances in which they might be used. Their advantages and disadvantages.

kcs.title: Standard error, estimator, bias
kcs.statement: Concepts of standard error, estimator, bias.
kcs.raw: Concepts of standard error, estimator, bias.
kcs.guidance: The sample mean, $\bar{x}$, and the sample variance, $s^2 = \dfrac{1}{n-1}\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar{x})^2$, as unbiased estimates of the corresponding population parameters.

kcs.title: Distribution of the sample mean
kcs.statement: The distribution of the sample mean $\bar{X}$.
kcs.raw: The distribution of the sample mean X .
kcs.guidance: $\bar X$ has mean $\mu$ and variance $\dfrac{\sigma^2}{n}$. If $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)$ then $\bar X \sim N\left(\mu, \dfrac{\sigma^2}{n}\right)$. No proofs required.

kcs.title: Confidence interval concept
kcs.statement: Concept of a confidence interval and its interpretation.
kcs.raw: Concept of a confidence interval and its interpretation.

kcs.title: Confidence interval for a Normal mean
kcs.statement: Confidence limits for a Normal mean, with variance known.
kcs.raw: Confidence limits for a Normal mean, with variance known.
kcs.guidance: Students will be expected to know how to apply the Normal distribution and use the standard error and obtain confidence intervals for the mean, rather than be concerned with any theoretical derivations.

kcs.title: Hypothesis test for a Normal mean
kcs.statement: Hypothesis tests for the mean of a Normal distribution with variance known.
kcs.raw: Hypothesis tests for the mean of a Normal distribution with variance known.

kcs.title: Central Limit Theorem for large samples
kcs.statement: Use of Central Limit theorem to extend hypothesis tests and confidence intervals to samples from non-Normal distributions. Use of large sample results to extend to the case in which the variance is unknown.
kcs.raw: Use of Central Limit theorem to extend hypothesis tests and confidence intervals to samples from non-Normal distributions. Use of large sample results to extend to the case in which the variance is unknown.
kcs.guidance: $\dfrac{\bar X - \mu}{S/\sqrt{n}}$ can be treated as $N(0,1)$ when $n$ is large. A knowledge of the $t$-distribution is not required.

kcs.title: Comparing two Normal means, variances known
kcs.statement: Hypothesis test for the difference between the means of two Normal distributions with variances known.
kcs.raw: Hypothesis test for the difference between the means of two Normal distributions with variances known.

kcs.title: Comparing two means, variances unknown
kcs.statement: Use of large sample results to extend to the case in which the population variances are unknown.
kcs.raw: Use of large sample results to extend to the case in which the population variances are unknown.
kcs.guidance: Use of $\dfrac{(\bar X - \bar Y) - (\mu_x - \mu_y)}{\sqrt{\dfrac{S_x^2}{n_x} + \dfrac{S_y^2}{n_y}}} \sim N(0,1)$. A knowledge of the $t$-distribution is not required.

kcs.title: Chi-squared goodness of fit statistic
kcs.statement: The null and alternative hypotheses. The use of $\sum_{i=1}^n \dfrac{(O_i - E_i)^2}{E_i}$ as an approximate $\chi^2$ statistic.
kcs.raw: The null and alternative hypotheses. ( O E ) 2 n − ∑ The use of as an i i E i = 1 i approximate χ2 statistic.
kcs.guidance: Applications to include the discrete uniform, binomial, Normal, Poisson and continuous uniform (rectangular) distributions. Lengthy calculations will not be required.

kcs.title: Degrees of freedom
kcs.guidance: Students will be expected to determine the degrees of freedom when one or more parameters are estimated from the data. Cells should be combined when $E_i < 5$. Yates' correction is not required.

kcs.title: Spearman's rank correlation
kcs.statement: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient, its use, interpretation and limitations.
kcs.raw: Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient, its use, interpretation and limitations.
kcs.guidance: Numerical questions involving ties will not be set. Some understanding of how to deal with ties will be expected.

kcs.title: Testing for zero correlation
kcs.statement: Testing the hypothesis that a correlation is zero.
kcs.raw: Testing the hypothesis that a correlation is zero.
kcs.guidance: Use of tables for Spearman's and product moment correlation coefficients.
